tool.name: PlasBench align
tool.description: predicted plasmids to a complete reference with minimap2

param.name: reference
param.label: Complete reference assembly
param.help: The long-read or hybrid assembly used as ground truth. Must be the same reference the truth labels describe.

param.name: prediction
param.label: Predicted-plasmid FASTA
param.help: The sequence one reconstruction tool considers plasmid.

param.name: preset
param.label: minimap2 preset
param.option: asm5 — assembly to reference, up to ~5% divergence

param.name: ambiguity
param.label: Also emit an all-mappings PAF
param.help: Retains secondary alignments in a second file. PlasBench score uses it only to report repeated sequence mapping to both plasmid and chromosome; it never changes F1.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Aligns a predicted-plasmid FASTA to the complete reference with minimap2 and emits the PAF that **PlasBench score** consumes.
This is a deliberately thin wrapper: it fixes the invocation the PlasBench pipeline itself uses (``--secondary=no -c -x asm5``) so that a Galaxy workflow and a command-line run project predictions onto the reference the same way. If the alignment step differs, the scores are not comparable.
**Why two PAFs?**
The primary PAF drops secondary alignments and is what scoring uses. The optional all-mappings PAF keeps them, and lets scoring report how much predicted sequence is repetitive enough to map to both plasmid and chromosome. That figure is a diagnostic only — it never alters precision, recall or F1.
**Next step**
Feed the PAF, the same predicted FASTA, and the truth labels to **PlasBench score**.
